objectives: LO 3.1.1: Describe common stock, its main types (blue-chip, growth, income, value, cyclical, defensive, technology), its risks, and rights vs. warrants
LO 3.2.1: Explain how cash dividends, DRIPs, stock dividends, splits and reverse splits affect shareholders, basis and the company
LO 3.3.1: Compare open-end funds (NAV, share classes, expenses, fund objectives, taxation), closed-end funds, UITs and separately managed accounts
LO 3.4.1: Describe ETFs, hedge funds, funds of funds and GICs and who each suits
LO 3.5.1: Calculate average cost per share under dollar cost averaging, value averaging and share averaging, and fund basis under each basis method
LO 3.6.1: Use objectives, holdings, manager flexibility, performance, fees, turnover, size, age and tax efficiency to select funds
synthesis: This module turns the risk and return tools from earlier modules into product choices: which stock type, which pooled vehicle, and which share class fits a client. Distribution and basis rules link directly to tax planning (qualified dividends, capital gain distributions, basis methods), while averaging techniques and fund-selection screens feed portfolio construction and asset allocation. In client work the same screens (expense ratio, turnover, tax efficiency and a fund's real, not labeled, allocation) decide which funds earn a place in a plan.

example.title: Dollar cost averaging: average cost vs. average price
example.html:
Jun invests $3,000 a month for four months at prices of $20, $15, $24 and $16.

MonthPriceShares
1$20150.0
2$15200.0
3$24125.0
4$16187.5
Total662.5

Average cost = $12,000 ÷ 662.5 = $18.11. Average price = ($20 + $15 + $24 + $16) ÷ 4 = $18.75. The fixed dollar amount bought more shares when the price was low, so cost is $0.64 below the average price. At the final $16 price the account is worth $10,600 — a $1,400 loss, so DCA lowers cost but does not guarantee a profit.

keyNumbers: More than 60 days in the 121-day window starting 60 days before ex-date (2026 edition figure)
Small up to $2B; mid $2B–$10B; large over $10B
May be waived after about 5 years
mustKnow: Buy before the ex-dividend date to get a declared dividend
Stock dividends and splits: no tax, same total value and basis, lower basis per share
NAV per share = (assets − liabilities) ÷ shares; forward pricing at the next NAV
Closed-end funds trade at a premium or discount to NAV; open-end funds trade at NAV (+ load)
DCA average cost = total dollars ÷ total shares, which is below the simple average price
Basis = price + commissions + reinvested distributions; specific ID most favorable, FIFO the default
Expense ratio excludes loads and trading costs; turnover = lesser of buys or sells ÷ average assets
traps: Reinvested dividends and capital gain distributions are still taxable (constructive receipt)
Value averaging can require selling; DCA and share averaging never do
'No-load' funds may still charge 12b-1 fees (hidden loads)
A fund labeled 'stock' may hold cash or foreign stocks: check manager flexibility
tips: For split questions, total value never changes; only the share count and price per share do
On basis-method questions in a rising market: specific ID gives the lowest gain, FIFO the highest
Match the fund to the client's top-priority objective first, then risk tolerance, then cost and taxes
